text:
Charlie Coyle is playing the biggest role of his career in Columbus, close to 20 minutes a night, and the Blue Jackets are dominating the play with him on: 57% of the expected goals at five on five, 12.6 points better than without him. He even got the revenge game, a four-point night against the Avalanche team that traded him.

The scoring hasn't matched it yet. Thirteen points in 16 games is fine, but Columbus has scored almost four fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on, and his own finishing is a goal and a half under expectation. Our numbers have him adding only 0.05 wins through his goals so far, near the bottom of the league. That should turn.

Evolving-Hockey had him 58th of 401 forwards in wins above replacement last season, with a caveat: strong linemates flattered his raw numbers. He's a setup man in Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking. Our range puts him at 54 to 79 points.
